assignment_name: FIT1049_S1_2021-Assignment 1 Part A - Individual research report (Weight 10%)-8256821
title: Career research report (FIT1049 A1 Part A)
scale_note: The rubric gives criterion weights only; levels use HD 80-100%, D 70-80%, C 60-70%, P 50-60%, N 30-50%, F 0-30% of the weight.

levels.label: Exemplary (HD)
levels.description: ≥10 highly relevant, authoritative sources spanning academic, industry and governmental material; evidence of meticulous selection strategy.

levels.label: High (D)
levels.description: 8–9 strong sources; minor gaps but role and industry still comprehensively covered.

levels.label: Credit (C)
levels.description: 6–7 acceptable sources; noticeable but non-critical gaps or slight over-reliance on a single source type.

levels.label: Pass (P)
levels.description: 5 sources; coverage adequate yet limited in scope or variety.

levels.label: Needs Improvement (N)
levels.description: 3–4 weak or marginal sources; significant blind spots in discussion.

levels.label: Unsatisfactory (F)
levels.description: ≤2 sources or sources of dubious credibility.

levels.label: Exemplary (HD)
levels.description: Critical synthesis leads to novel insights; arguments consistently data-driven and nuanced; clear linkage between evidence and claims.

levels.label: High (D)
levels.description: Critical discussion with occasional fresh perspectives; argument mostly data-driven.

levels.label: Credit (C)
levels.description: Mostly descriptive but shows intermittent critical reflection; logic generally sound.

levels.label: Pass (P)
levels.description: Predominantly descriptive; minimal critique; basic logical structure.

levels.label: Needs Improvement (N)
levels.description: Superficial treatment; fragmented or unsupported assertions.

levels.label: Unsatisfactory (F)
levels.description: No discernible analysis; copy-paste of factual snippets.

levels.label: Exemplary (HD)
levels.description: Logical, reader-centred flow; headings, figures and tables used expertly; flawless adherence to formatting rules.

levels.label: High (D)
levels.description: Clear organisation; minor lapses in formatting do not impede comprehension.

levels.label: Credit (C)
levels.description: Overall structure evident though transitions may be abrupt; occasional formatting issues.

levels.label: Pass (P)
levels.description: Acceptable structure but inconsistent formatting or missing elements (e.g. figure captions).

levels.label: Needs Improvement (N)
levels.description: Disorganised; formatting errors distract reader.

levels.label: Unsatisfactory (F)
levels.description: Lacks coherent structure.

levels.label: Exemplary (HD)
levels.description: Sophisticated yet concise language; zero grammatical or typographical errors.

levels.label: High (D)
levels.description: Professional language; ≤2 minor errors.

levels.label: Credit (C)
levels.description: Minor errors (≤4) but meaning always clear.

levels.label: Pass (P)
levels.description: Frequent minor errors or a few major errors that momentarily impede reading.

levels.label: Needs Improvement (N)
levels.description: Numerous errors impede comprehension.

levels.label: Unsatisfactory (F)
levels.description: Language so flawed that meaning is obscured.

levels.label: Exemplary (HD)
levels.description: All in-text citations and reference list entries perfect per APA 7th.

levels.label: High (D)
levels.description: 1–2 very minor inconsistencies.

levels.label: Credit (C)
levels.description: Several consistent but non-critical deviations (e.g. missing DOIs).

levels.label: Pass (P)
levels.description: Many instances of incorrect punctuation/order; still recognisably APA.

levels.label: Needs Improvement (N)
levels.description: Citations frequently missing or incorrect; risk of academic integrity concerns.

levels.label: Unsatisfactory (F)
levels.description: References absent or unusable.
